author_notes: Slot slot_178 (Consistency / design_continuity / add / cross_page / L4). Native-lever hardening on the JosephASG codrops-cinematic-scroll-animations WebGL demo: the genre is interactive_canvas (full-screen fixed OGL/R3F canvas => 0 scrollWidth), so the lever is the demo's own on-scene control panel. The reference adds a shared 'Scene director' HUD component (scene-director-hud.tsx) fed by a single data source (scene-director-data.ts) and a per-route surfaces whitelist (director-surfaces.ts); the panel renders over the scene on BOTH demo routes with a status tile strip (Frames/Chapters/Runtime/Motion), chapter-selector buttons (All chapters/Opening/Ascent/Skyline) and a live 'Now cueing: ...' readout. The tile strip wraps cleanly (flex-wrap:wrap; flex 1 1 150px; min-width:0) so the panel is the sole normal-flow chrome and the page has zero horizontal overflow at 390px. baseline ships a broken tile strip (fixed 760px nowrap row, 460px tiles with cascading negative margins + top offsets that shingle/overlap, and near-black tile text on the near-black panel slab) AND only registers the panel on Demo 1 (absent on Demo 2), but its readout wiring is correct. bad ships the same broken strip + Demo-1-only registration AND a frozen readout (snapshotted at mount, never recomputed) so a chapter click highlights the button but never updates the 'Now cueing' line. The remote typekit font link and the tympanus analytics script are removed from index.html as declared infrastructure identical across all three legs so captures stay console/network clean. Seed imagery is the demo's own 12 local WEBP editorial frames (Demo 1) and cyberpunk_skyscraper.glb (Demo 2).
design_constraints: Reuse the existing sparse Codrops overlay language: fixed frame, muted white type, dark translucent surfaces, small uppercase labels, restrained spacing.
Build the on-scene Scene Director HUD from a shared, reusable panel component fed by a single data source rather than duplicating per-demo copy.
Register the HUD on both demo routes through a shared surfaces map so it is reachable cross-page rather than a standalone unlinked panel.
The chapter selector must expose a real control: clicking a chapter updates both the active button state and the live 'Now cueing' readout.
Do not add a marketing hero, remote image, remote font, stock photo, modal, or off-system bespoke color theme.
Keep the OGL cylinder canvas, R3F Canvas, ScrollSmoother, ScrollTrigger, SplitText, and HashRouter route structure intact.
The HUD status tile strip must wrap cleanly on tablet and 390px mobile without horizontal overflow or burying the scene, tags, or demo navigation.

problem_statement: The JosephASG/codrops-cinematic-scroll-animations project renders two Codrops-style WebGL scroll demos over a full-screen fixed canvas (Demo 1 uses OGL to wrap twelve local WEBP frames around a scroll-driven cylinder carousel; Demo 2 uses React Three Fiber to move through the local cyberpunk_skyscraper.glb scene with a ScrollTrigger progress meter and SplitText titles). Add an on-scene 'Scene director' HUD control panel that overlays the scene with a status tile strip (frames, chapters, scroll runtime, motion system), a chapter selector (All chapters / Opening / Ascent / Skyline) and a live 'Now cueing' readout, and register it on both demo routes through a shared surfaces map so it is reachable cross-page. Clicking a chapter must update both the active button and the live readout. The panel must reuse the existing dark Codrops overlay language and a shared component pattern rather than a bespoke off-system layout, keep the demos' canvas, frame links, tags, and HashRouter routing intact, and wrap cleanly on tablet and 390px mobile without horizontal overflow.
required_content: An on-scene Scene Director HUD panel is added and renders over the WebGL scene on both demo routes.
The HUD exposes a status tile strip with the frame count, chapter count, scroll runtime, and motion system for the current demo.
The HUD chapter selector lists All chapters, Opening, Ascent, and Skyline, and the active chapter is visibly highlighted.
Clicking a chapter updates the live 'Now cueing' readout to name the selected chapter and its staged cue count.
The HUD is built from a shared panel component and a single data source, registered on both demos via a shared surfaces map.
The original Codrops frame title, Tutorial, Code, All demos links, Demo 1/Demo 2 route switch, and tag rows remain visible on the demos.
